approved_payload.content: Police officers attached to Polokwane International Airport were arrested by the Limpopo Provincial Anti-Corruption Unit, assisted by the Polokwane Tactical Response Team, on the evening of Monday 19 October (Review Online, 19 and 20 October). Police first said five were arrested, then corrected this: three (two men and a woman aged 44 to 49) were arrested and two colleagues were still being sought (police statement via Review Online, 20 October). On Tuesday 20 October five SAPS members attached to the airport appeared in the Polokwane Magistrate's Court on charges of defeating the ends of justice and contravening section 49 of the Immigration Act, and were granted bail of R1,000 each; the case was postponed to 30 November for further investigation (Review Online, 21 October). The case is about an older incident. According to police, on 17 April 2025 a traffic officer stopped a minibus carrying 46 undocumented foreign nationals on the N1 near Polokwane; police allege that four male officers and one female officer from the airport arrived, said the station commander had arranged for the passengers to be taken to Polokwane police station, and that neither the officers nor the passengers could later be found there. These are allegations: no one has been convicted, and the accused are not named here. Case status: accused, on bail, next court date 30 November 2026. All three reports come from one outlet and rest on police statements. The pin marks the airport, where the arrests took place and where the officers work, not the April 2025 roadside stop.
